risk_findings: Data retention ambiguity: conflicting statements about post-termination retention (30 days deletion vs. up to 90 days in backups) create uncertainty about residual customer data exposure and contractual compliance.

Model training and data use ambiguity: one document asserts customer data is not used to train foundation models while another permits use of de-identified/aggregated customer-derived data for model evaluation/tuning, raising risks around re-identification, consent, and contractual/regulated-data use.

Human-review coverage gap: documents conflict on whether all AI-generated recommendations are human-reviewed; selective review may allow automated recommendations to drive downstream actions without human oversight.
Key management and backup controls undocumented: vendor-managed encryption keys and lack of documented rotation/HSM/backups practices increase cryptographic and recovery risk.
uncertainties: Whether 'deleted within 30 days' applies to backups or only primary systems and how deletion is implemented and validated.
The exact definitions and de-identification techniques applied to 'de-identified or aggregated customer-derived data' and whether such data may be shared externally or used to train models.
The criteria, percentage, and workflow for 'selected' AI-generated recommendations that receive human review and what downstream actions are allowed without review.
Details of key management (KMS/HSM usage, rotation schedule, access controls) and backup encryption practices.

conflicting_claims: ClearPath_Test_Security_Overview(1).txt: 'Production data is deleted within 30 days after contract termination.'
ClearPath_Conflicting_Evidence.docx: 'Customer data may be retained in encrypted backup systems for up to 90 days after contract termination before full backup rotation is completed.'
document_conflicts.explanation: One document states production data is deleted within 30 days; the other indicates backups may retain customer data for up to 90 days post-termination. These claims are materially inconsistent regarding residual retention timelines and should be reconciled against contractual obligations and technical backup processes.

document_conflicts.topic: Use of customer data for model training and improvement
conflicting_claims: ClearPath_Test_Security_Overview(1).txt: 'Customer data is not used to train foundation models.'

ClearPath_Conflicting_Evidence.docx: 'Production data is not intentionally used to train foundation models.' and 'De-identified or aggregated customer-derived data may be used for internal model evaluation, performance tuning, and product improvement.'
document_conflicts.explanation: One document gives an absolute denial of use for training; the other qualifies that training is not intentional while permitting de-identified/aggregated customer-derived data for evaluation/tuning. These are materially different positions about permissible data uses and risk to customer-derived data.

document_conflicts.topic: Scope of human review for AI-generated recommendations
conflicting_claims: ClearPath_Test_Security_Overview(1).txt: 'Human staff review AI-generated recommendations before taking action.'
ClearPath_Conflicting_Evidence.docx: 'Human staff review selected AI-generated recommendations, but not every recommendation requires manual review before downstream action.'
document_conflicts.explanation: One document implies all AI-generated recommendations are reviewed prior to action; the other specifies only selected recommendations are reviewed. This affects the level of human oversight and potential for automated actions without review.

follow_up_questions: Provide the formal data retention and deletion policy covering primary systems and backups, and confirm maximum post-termination retention period for all customer data (including backups).

Clarify whether any customer-derived data (including de-identified/aggregated data) is used for model training or external model improvement, and describe de-identification methods and risk assessments performed.
Describe the human-review policy: criteria for selecting recommendations for review, percent or volume reviewed, roles responsible, and whether any categories of recommendations are auto-executed.
Provide documented key management details: whether keys are stored in a KMS/HSM, rotation schedule, access controls, and backup encryption practices.
human_review_notes: Verify and reconcile conflicting retention and data-use claims across documents; obtain contractual commitments (SLA/contract language) and technical evidence (backup configs, deletion logs, snapshots) to confirm actual retention behavior.

Assess privacy/regulatory implications of permitted use of de-identified/aggregated data (re-identification risk, consent, and any required DTA/BAA). Request technical description of de-identification and data flows for model evaluation.

Evaluate operational risk from selective human review by requesting metrics on review coverage and examples of automated downstream actions. Confirm mitigating controls (alerts, escalation, audit trails).
Request and review key-management documentation (KMS/HSM architecture diagrams, access policies, rotation records) and proof of encryption/enforced controls for backups.
